problem: Prior ALFRED agents (flat policies or hybrid map-based ones) often plan sub-goals with task-irrelevant objects and forget object state changes (already relocated objects, changed appearance/occlusion, sliced objects), causing interaction and navigation failures, especially in unseen environments.
motivation: Household tasks require planning step by step while accounting for the consequences of earlier actions. Templated approaches (FILM, Prompter) need hand-designed templates for each task type, while learned planners confuse which objects to interact with. The paper observes that task-relevant objects are shared across all sub-goals and that spatial memory lacks object-state information.
key_idea: Predict task-relevant objects (context) explicitly and fill them into object-agnostic sub-goal frames, and maintain an environment-aware memory of object masks, relocations and changed-state locations on top of a semantic spatial map.
insight: Ablation shows both modules matter and are complementary: removing CAP costs 2.34 (seen) / 3.86 (unseen) SR, removing EAM costs 5.35 / 4.45 SR, and removing both is worst. The CAP gain is not due to model size: a 651M no-context LSTM planner (74.91 unseen plan accuracy) is no better than a 165M one (74.18), while the 713M CAP planner reaches 77.34. Explicitly predicting the context makes the agent less rigid than templates and generalizes better, with a smaller seen-unseen gap.
method: Context predictor: three fine-tuned BERT predictors output the main object c_O, carrier/container c_M and destination receptacle c_R from the instruction (may be None).
Sub-goal frame sequence generator: generates sub-goal frames (action, <O>, <R>) using meta-classes x_O, x_M, x_R, which are then replaced by the predicted context objects to form the final sub-goals.

Detailed planners: one self-attention LSTM per sub-goal action type, supervised, that maps a sub-goal to executable (action, object) sequences (e.g. Pickup(Plate, Cabinet) becomes Open, Pickup, Close).
Semantic spatial map: back-projects predicted depth and object masks into 3D world coordinates to build a top-down semantic map with obstacles and objects.
Retrospective Object Recognition: keeps the latest object masks and reuses them when the same object is being interacted with but the mask predictor fails (e.g. occlusion).
Object Relocation Tracking: stores the latest 2D location of each relocated object and excludes it from future navigation targets, avoiding re-moving the same object.
Object Location Caching: caches 2D locations and masks of objects whose state changed (e.g. sliced apple) so the agent can navigate back and interact without re-exploring.
Action policy: deterministic Fast Marching Method path planning on the discrete grid with an expanded obstacle map.

setting.backbone: BERT (fine-tuned) context predictors + LSTM sub-goal frame generator and detailed planners (trained), plus learned depth and mask predictors; FMM deterministic navigation
setting.training_data: ALFRED training split (expert demonstrations and language annotations); no extra data reported
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 300x300 (depth and masks predicted by models), language goal statement with or without step-by-step low-level instructions
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete actions (MoveAhead, Rotate 90°, Look 15°, 7 interaction actions with object masks, Stop)
setting.privileged: none (a variant uses hand-designed templated action sequences from FILM)

numbers_note: ALFRED is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is tagged other:ALFRED. PLW scores are reported as PLWSR and PLWGC. The ablation on test splits (Table 2) is not repeated here.
results: Without templates and with low-level instructions, CAPEAM reaches 46.11 SR on test-unseen (vs LGS-RPA 35.41) and 51.79 on test-seen. With the goal statement only it gets 43.69 unseen SR vs EPA 36.07 and 16.29 for HLSM. The paper claims up to +10.70% unseen SR over prior work. With templated actions it beats Prompter on unseen SR (45.72 vs 42.64 without low-level instructions; 49.84 vs 45.72 with) but trails it on seen.
limitations: Context is fixed at the start of a task and cannot adapt if the context changes during execution.
Pipeline relies on predicted depth and mask models and hand-crafted FMM navigation; PLW efficiency lags LGS-RPA, which uses extra human-in-the-loop data.
Evaluated only on ALFRED (simulation) with no real-robot tests.
